title: The Royal Rivalry, Episode 3: Picking Up the Pieces (full episode)
series: The Royal Rivalry (Clash of Clans fan comic), full episodes

lines: Previously, on The Royal Rivalry. A storm came out of a clear sky, and an Electro Dragon tore through the kingdom.
The King and Queen fought the dragon, and each other. And the Grand Warden fell.
The Warden had saved the kingdom. Now someone had to save him.
The sun rose over a kingdom that looked very different from the day before.
The new wall was rubble. The Archer Tower was a stump. And the fountain, somehow, was the only thing still standing.
In the Healer's house, the Grand Warden had not moved all night.
His heart is strong. But the lightning is still inside him. I can feel it crackling.
Outside her door, the King and Queen had not moved all night either.
You should go and get some sleep.
You should go and get some sleep.
Neither of them went to get some sleep.
At dawn, the Healer opened her door.
Get in here. Both of you. Quietly.
They both tried to go through the door at the same time. Quietly.
The Healer raised her hands, and golden light filled the room. Brighter. And brighter.
Come back to us, old man. This kingdom is not finished with you.
Warden, we're so sorry. We should have listened.
I should have listened. Me. More sorry. Much more sorry.
Stop. Both of you. I am far too tired for an apology competition.
But an apology competition was exactly what happened next. Out in the square, the whole village was waiting.
The Queen's arrow hit our King!
The King's barrel hit our Queen!
If she had listened to me for one second!
If he had ever once made a plan!
And just like that, they were arguing again. Louder than ever.
Excuse me. Excuse me! The Town Hall is on fire. A little bit. Mostly the curtains.
The Wizard tried to put the fire out with a spell. It was the wrong spell.
That's... a bigger fire. Hold on. I know this one. I definitely know this one.
In the end, the Archers put it out with buckets.
Fixing the kingdom was slow work. The Barbarians carried stones. The Archers carried water.
Around noon, a row of small green heads appeared over the broken wall. The goblins were back.
We came back for the snacks. And also, uh...
Even I wouldn't do this to a kingdom. And I'm a professional.
That evening, the King found a sack by the gate. Inside was half of the stolen gold, and a muddy note.
Storms are bad for business. Get well soon, old man. Love, the Goblins.
The King lifted beams that four Barbarians together couldn't move.
The Queen climbed the broken tower, and shot ropes across the gaps, so the builders could cross.
Then the old Archer Tower began to creak. And a young Barbarian was standing right beneath it.
Uh. Is it supposed to lean like that?
The tower fell. The King dived under it, and caught it on his shoulders.
But it was too heavy, even for him.
From the wall, the Queen fired three arrows, each one trailing a rope, and pinned the tower to the ground.
Hold it steady! Don't you dare drop it!
The young Barbarian scrambled free. The tower settled with a thud.
And for one moment, the King and the Queen looked at each other. It almost looked like teamwork.
That's my natural colour when I'm winning.
Down in the square, something even stranger happened. A Barbarian sat down next to an Archer, and held out half of his skewer.
You carried water all day. You must be starving.
Thanks. You carried stones all day. You must be... very strong.
That afternoon, the Queen went back to the place where the lightning had struck the Warden.
Burned into the stones was a strange mark. A bolt of lightning, inside two rings.
It was still crackling. Still warm. A whole day later, it should have been cold.
Lightning doesn't leave a signature. Unless someone wants you to know who sent it.
She wasn't the only one interested in the mark. From behind a pile of rubble, a small green face was watching.
You. You're the goblin who stole our gold.
Before she could grab him, he snatched up a scorched blue dragon scale, and ran.
The Queen chased him through the ruins, over the rubble, and straight into the King.
I see stars. Lots of stars.
The goblin was long gone. But he had dropped something as he ran.
A crumpled map, with the very same mark drawn on it. Far beyond the hills.
Dropped very neatly. Almost as if someone wanted it to be found.
Goblin! Come out! We just want to talk!
Strangely, the goblin did not come out.
Why would a goblin have a map with that mark on it?
Because someone paid him to go there.
For once, I agree with you.
That evening, the Warden was well enough to sit up in bed. They brought him the map.
Long before this kingdom, before the walls, before either of you arrived half a step apart, this valley belonged to no one.
There was a sorceress who ruled them. She did not want gold. She wanted Elixir.
Every drop of it, to make her storm grow bigger. And bigger. And bigger.
The Storm Sorceress. My grandmother used to tell me stories about her. I thought they were only stories.
She said the Sorceress could ride the lightning itself. That her castle was built from clouds. And that she never, ever forgot a face.
Your grandmother was a very wise woman.
I fought her once, with this very book. I did not defeat her. I only sent her far away.
And I was much younger then.
Then we fight her again. I'll go tomorrow. Alone, if I have to.
You'll get lost before lunch. I'll go.
Neither of you is going anywhere. Not like this.
She sent one dragon, and it broke us. Not because it was strong. Because you two were busy fighting each other.
Nobody said anything for a long time.
Rest. All of you. Tomorrow, we make a plan. Together.
Plans are for people who can't...
Finish that sentence, and I will hit you with this book.
When the heroes had gone, the Healer sat down beside the Warden's bed.
You didn't tell them everything, did you?
No. Not yet. They are not ready to hear the rest.
And when will they be ready?
When they can stand in the same room without shouting.
That night, neither hero could sleep. Again.
The King sat on the edge of the fountain, which was, of course, still standing.
The Queen sat on the wall, polishing her crossbow for the forty-first time.
The King remembered the day they arrived. Two strangers, at the very same gate, at the very same moment.
Back then, there had been no walls to guard, and no gold to argue over. Just a little camp, and one old man who believed in them both.
Today, with the tower. That was... not terrible.
Not terrible at all. I mean, I had it.
Then the Elixir collectors began to hum. All of them, at once.
Oh no. Oh no, no, no. It's fizzing again!
Nobody stopped to wonder what the Wizard was doing out by the collectors, in the middle of the night.
Every drop of Elixir in the kingdom was glowing, and tugging, as if it wanted to fly away.
The Queen climbed to the top of the broken tower, and looked where the Elixir was pointing.
Far beyond the hills, high in the night sky, the clouds had formed a shape. A castle. Made of storm.
King. You need to come up here and see this.
It's so much worse than a goblin.
And at the very top of the storm castle, two eyes opened. And looked straight back at them.
To be continued. The Storm Sorceress is coming. Is the kingdom ready? Tell me in the comments.
